protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for DR-007 under adopted D-054 / D-057
verdictBasis: The recording itself is sound: every digest and commit verifies, the Route A remainder and owner role are exact matches against their sources, DR-007 stays HARD-BLOCKED, no D9 code is invented, and no other row is touched. The single SHOULD-FIX is that the D-057 clause-3 section has been thinned relative to every adopted sibling, dropping one element D-057 enumerates by name and one that the entry's own clause 4 makes necessary.

shouldFixRecorded.finding: Three elements present in all four sibling owner-recording drafts are absent here. I tested this draft-to-draft rather than against the condensed COORD entries, which summarise rather than reproduce these sections. D-060, D-061, D-065 and D-077 turn 2 each carry all three; D-078 carries none.

parts.detail: D-057's adopted decision text enumerates 'pins for the D-054 user-amendment path and sha256'. D-078 gives the commit and the sha256 but the string 'D-054.user-amendment.md' occurs zero times in the file. This is a literal miss against a named D-057 requirement, and 'missing D-057 dependency pins' is an attack axis of this dispatch. A digest with no path does not tell a reader which file to measure.
parts.severityNote: compliance rather than substance — I independently verified the amendment by its digest, so the authority chain is real

parts.element: the MF-6 reconciliation limb of the overturn procedure
parts.detail: Every sibling reads 'Compound. Overturn: C-D0NN, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note.' D-078 reads 'Compound. Overturn: C-D078.' — the limb is gone. This is the substantive part of the finding, because clause 4 of this very entry states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)', deferring a cell note to a separate later act exactly as its siblings do. So the entry creates a dependent MF-6 obligation and then omits it from its own reversal procedure. D-000 clause 3 lists the overturn procedure among the mandatory recorded elements, and D-054's Mechanics section assigns 'reversibility over every dependent recording' to D-057.
parts.severityNote: substantive: an overturn procedure that does not reach an obligation the entry itself creates

parts.element: the revocation/supersession sentence on the dependency declaration
parts.detail: Siblings read 'Dependencies: … Revocation or overturn requires this owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes.' D-078 reads 'Dependencies: D-054, D-057, D-071, and D-075.' and stops. This is the same omission as (b) seen from the dependency side.
parts.severityNote: closely coupled to (b); one repair fixes both

shouldFixRecorded.examinedAndNotIncluded: The readiness effect also drops 'Conditions 2–5 unchanged', which the siblings carry. I did not include it: clause 3 states 'Conditions 2–5 remain', so the substance is present elsewhere in the entry and nothing is lost.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: Nothing asserted is false and the recording is otherwise complete and correct. The authority chain resolves — I verified the D-054 amendment, both selection and coordinator-recording commits, the disposition and both verdicts — and an overturn could still be executed, just without the entry naming the dependent note it defers.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: Restore the sibling form: pin the D-054 path alongside its sha256 and commit; restore 'Revocation or overturn requires this owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes.' to the dependency declaration; and restore 'plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note' to the Reversibility clause.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. The DR-007-specific risks all fail: no D9 code is invented, the D9 successor and retention-loss integration stay owed, DR-114 and DR-G21 ride reduced-or-wait, and DR-007 stays HARD-BLOCKED as file 08 confirms. Six digests and five commits verify, the Route A remainder is an exact three-item match against the pinned disposition, and the owner role matches file 08 character for character. My objection is that the D-057 pin section has been thinned relative to every adopted sibling: the D-054 path that D-057 names explicitly is gone, and so is the MF-6 reconciliation limb of the overturn — which matters because clause 4 of this entry is what creates the deferred MF-6 note in the first place.
objections: C2-D078-SF1 — D-057 pin section thinned: missing D-054 user-amendment path, missing MF-6 reconciliation in overturn, missing revocation/supersession sentence.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: cbe31fc6f04789b6faeee82c2efd0652f5910647c98813ccfdf30088b630b4e3, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at f4184bab55bc6870afca039e12e1cfa0d67f6aa81956bae070c310b75729504f, equal to both the dispatch and the prompt. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The finding rests on a draft-to-draft comparison, which is the correct comparison class. I first checked the adopted COORD entries and found none of them carries the D-054 path or the revocation sentence — but that is because COORD entries are condensed summaries, not reproductions of the pin section. Comparing the drafts instead, D-060, D-061, D-065 and D-077 turn 2 each carry the D-054 path, the revocation sentence, the MF-6 reconciliation limb and 'Conditions 2–5 unchanged'; D-078 carries none of the four. I corrected my own comparison before grading rather than filing against the wrong baseline.

The D-057 requirement is literal, not inferred. Its adopted decision text reads 'pins for the D-054 user-amendment path and sha256, D-054/D-057/Route B IDs and commits, disposition and verdicts, owner role, preview scope, Route A remainder, and every operative rider.' Of that list, D-078 supplies everything except the path.

The attack 'invents D9 codes' fails. Clause 3 states 'Invents no D9 code', the Route A remainder owes 'Reviewed retention degradation/refusal integration without invented codes', and the ride disclosure states doctor's D9 mapping (DR-114) and DR-G21 goldens 'ship reduced, re-scoped, or wait'. That tracks the pinned disposition, whose own text I verified in its review cycle.

The Route A remainder is complete, tested by string equality against the disposition's whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA: three items each, exact match, same order — the D9 successor to v1.14 closing observation→faultCause, optional presence and the success/policy/interrupted branch; reviewed retention degradation/refusal integration without invented codes; and independent review of that successor.
The owner role is an exact string match: file 08's DR-007 owner cell reads 'D9 authority + evidence/retention owner' and the entry pins the identical string.

'Operative riders: none' is correct and I can confirm half of it absolutely: my own DR-007 verdict at aa70e150… records ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories, so there is no advisory to classify on my side. The recital 'ACCEPT 0/0' matches.

The attack 'treats D-077 as not adopted or overturns it' fails. The entry states 'D-077 is ADOPTED at d401ecd8494cd3e1b5f7b3553d9d9e6fed4dd9e5 (DR-006 owner recording). It is not this file. This entry does not adopt or overturn D-077.' That commit resolves to 'D-077: owner-record DR-006 preview Route B disposition', and COORD carries D-077 as ADOPTED.

The attack 'bundles another row' fails: the protocol line states this file is one owner-recording entry and one cycle, the header states 'Does not owner-record DR-006, DR-009, or any other row', and clause 5 repeats it.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: the header refuses SATISFIED, clause 2 scopes any effect to 'architecture-preview scope only', clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-007 SATISFIED', and the readiness effect reads 'Zero SATISFIED'. file 08's DR-007 status cell still leads HARD-BLOCKED, so the premise holds.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses the implementation directory, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

All six cited digests match live bytes: COORD ac159ae3…, file 08 9495c70f…, the D-054 amendment c274d140…, the DR-007 v2 disposition 53b72a91…, my verdict aa70e150…, and the Codex verdict 807d0b63… (hashed, not opened).

All five cited commits resolve at full hash: 29670ed D-054, 33597e8 D-057, 5f6b4e07 D-071, 13ca9a71 D-075, and d401ecd8 D-077. The coordinator recording at 13ca9a71 is a separate commit from the selection at 5f6b4e07, satisfying D-057's prior-separately-committed precondition, and D-054, D-057, D-071 and D-075 are all live.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The recording is sound and the DR-007-specific traps are all avoided — no invented D9 code, the successor and retention integration left owed, the rides disclosed, the row still HARD-BLOCKED. What I cannot pass is the pin section, which has been thinned relative to every adopted sibling. Part (a) is a literal miss against D-057, which enumerates 'the D-054 user-amendment path and sha256' and gets only the sha256. Part (b) is the one that would actually bite: clause 4 defers a file 08 cell note under MF-6, and the overturn clause — alone among the siblings — does not mention reconciling it, so the entry creates an obligation its own reversal procedure does not reach. I note that I initially compared against the adopted COORD entries, found the elements absent there too, and had to correct myself: those entries are condensed summaries, and the drafts are the right baseline. On that baseline the four siblings are unanimous and this one is the outlier.
